reason: Retain V3A stack-parse-then-box allocation and fused Owned parser, with compact CachedSize32 and shared Wire windows.
V4 inline-hint split parser improves the wide RPC fixture but loses depth8 and depth64 parse/read-all against V3A; no universal dominance claim.
Owned profile removes repeated lazy descendant validation for read-all; lazy remains default because forwarding/cached encode and sparse access have different costs.
No benchmark identity or field-count thresholds were added. No further variants after V4.
measurement_limits: Shared-host paired diagnostics, not a world ranking.
Separate requested allocation bytes are not RSS.
Build elapsed times are provenance and cannot support codegen-speed claims.

limits: Closed-loop shared-host diagnostics; no open-loop SLO claim
No warmup qualification; pipeline percentile sample floor not met
Paired raw percentiles at each N; never subtract quantiles or pool repetitions

rejected_codegen.reason: All six cases regress warm process CPU in two paired shipping campaigns despite lower process RSS; no candidate shipped.

rejected_eager.reason: Full traversal improves6.38x but remains2.94xProst; partial64 CPU2.88x worse and requestedbytes464→5344. Storage layout does not shrink. Preserve as rejected experiment.

review.review_type: source inspection; no reviewer CPU tests or timing measurements
review.verdict: No blocking correctness, API compatibility or MSRV issue found in the inspected changes.
owned_profile_invariants: Default false leaves lazy selection and full-width cache unchanged; explicit false matches default output in consumer build checks.
Plugin parser, Config builder serialization, resolved state, worker apply and CodegenStateGuard reset carry the same owned flag.
Owned singular fields use existing Option<Box<T>> checked parser. Newly absent fields are installed only after successful merge; existing fields keep established partial-merge behavior.
Required-field initialization continues to follow the final merged tree. Existing required/oneof/group pathways are retained, and the consumer has independent Prost valid-value oracles.
Shared Wire propagation uses child input windows for singular/repeated LEN children and message-map values; it retains existing depth and UTF-8 validation.
Private compact-cache sizes below u32::MAX are exact. Sizes at or above the sentinel are cache misses and remain u64 computation results; no truncation or size limit is introduced.
Option<Box<T>> and AtomicU32 remain valid zero-initialized generated-field representations, as the existing Option/AtomicU64 layout does.
The compact cache maintains relaxed atomic synchronization, clone independence and cache-insensitive equality, matching the existing size-cache contract.
The inspected additions use stable APIs available in Rust1.85; executable MSRV validation is separate.
coalescer_invariants: The entire connection future is wrapped, including admission control; no request state or framing/flow-control parser was changed.
Notification before POLLING-clearing RMW is observed by that RMW; later notification sees POLLING clear and wakes parent itself.
Clearing an old notification immediately before polling is sound: that poll satisfies the prior notification; a concurrent or later notification sets NOTIFIED again.
A stable proxy waker is reused for the connection; parent registration updates task ownership on each poll.
At most four polls are processed per outer call, with early yield when Tokio cooperative budget is exhausted.
Ready and pinned Drop mark notifications closed and release retained parent before dropping transport/application state; later retained proxy wakers cannot recreate a parent reference.
No unsafe implementation, new dependency, per-RPC proxy allocation or unchecked memory operation was introduced.
test_scope_reviewed: Owned consumer checks storage profile output/reset, deterministic allocation work, compact layout, shared backing pointers, clone/mutation independence, failed merge state, unknown fields, strict UTF-8, truncation, depth, required merges, oneof replacement, maps and groups.
Server lifecycle/race tests cover external wake, latest parent, pending-boundary race, finite poll budget, Ready, Drop and poll panic.
limits: Finite source inspection is not exhaustive proof of arbitrary wire compatibility or a performance ranking.
This review did not duplicate owner test runs. Final integrated checks and exact-source benchmark binding remain separate.
The opt-in owned profile deliberately does more construction work than default lazy parsing; unchanged lazy forwarding can remain faster.

delta_from_reviewed_v4: Owned profile disables split_heavy and emits all field dispatch in the existing single match; default lazy selection remains unchanged.
Conditional Owned inline hint is removed because Owned no longer emits merge_heavy; the legacy helper keeps its original inline(never) annotation.
Stack parsing and Box installation on success, Cache32 and shared-wire windows are unchanged.
followup_review.assessment: No blocker. Both dispatch shapes call the same generated merge arms with the same depth, validation and final required checks. Message-set handling is unsplit in both shapes. The delta is code placement rather than new parsing semantics.
followup_review.validation: Read-only follow-up; exact-source integrated execution running separately under root.

docs_review.assessment: No material source/claim mismatch found. Docs distinguish explicit owned vs unchanged lazy default, shared-host paired measurements vs ranking, parse/full/partial/encoding work, requested allocation bytes vs RSS, and retained policy/feature gaps.
docs_review.draft_limits: Evidence packaging and final integrated-check results are still root work; no claim is made here that those pending outputs have completed.
